title: Influence and resampling disagreement
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set, let $\pi$ be a probability distribution on $\Omega$, and let $B$ be a finite Fourier basis of real-valued functions on $\Omega$ that is orthonormal for the $\pi$-weighted inner product and contains the constant-one function. For every natural number $n$, every function $f:\Omega^n\to\mathbb R$ taking only the values $-1$ and $1$, and every coordinate $i$, the influence of $f$ at $i$ equals twice the probability that replacing coordinate $i$ by an independent sample from $\pi$ changes the value of $f$, with the original input drawn from the product distribution $\pi^n$.
